page: Microsoft Azure D64lds_v6 is a compute-focused virtual machine belonging to the Dldsv6 server family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor with an x86_64 architecture, offering 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor operates at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz and features a 260 MB L3 cache. This instance is configured with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Local storage is provided via a bundled 3780 GB NVMe SSD.

In benchmark evaluations, the D64lds_v6 demonstrates strong capabilities across multiple compute and memory tasks. Single-core and multi-core CPU performance under stress-ng falls within the average range, while memory bandwidth tests show strong results, reaching 4425.91 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 254.01 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. The server excels in static web serving throughput and image processing, both ranking in the top tier. Cryptographic and database operations also register strong performance, with Redis SET operations achieving 83.04 million operations per second.

The primary architectural trade-off of the D64lds_v6 is its low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1:2. This design optimizes cost efficiency for compute-heavy workloads that do not require massive memory footprints, allowing users to leverage high CPU core counts without paying for unused RAM. However, memory-bound applications may face bottlenecks. The instance is suited for software compilation, web serving, database operations, and CPU-based machine learning inference, as evidenced by its strong prompt processing speeds on medium and large language models.
